_note: The noticeboard on the meetinghouse door (docs/15-regions.md, Noticeboards; decision 0401). Kettle Notch's board.json is the model and its note holds here: the seed picks a writer's line and fills {where} from `spots` and {in} from `places`; `pay` is the least and most each kind may pay, in item worth, and `npm run check` holds every payment to it. A writer must be in town at every hour, so the map's star is never wrong: Tamsin keeps to her table in the meetinghouse, the Shattucks to their yard. Benoni will be away a day, Coyle and Sukey go up Hobble Hill, and Hosea and Asa are from the road, so none of them write here. A line's `if` keeps it off the board while it wouldn't make sense (the wagon's list, once the wagon is empty). The Deep Cut is left out: it resets, and board work stays above ground.
gearHint: That's plain work, mind. The man minding the house for sale knows what plain work's worth. More than it is, likely.

words.thin: Clear two lots of creatures from {in}.
words.short: That's not all of them. I said {of}.
words.blurb: A notice on the meetinghouse door, from {name}. Pays {pay}.
words.fightBlurb: A notice on the meetinghouse door, from {name}. Pays {pay}. Creatures already seen off come back after a rest.

posted.text: SINGING SCHOOL will not meet this winter. Not enough for the parts. The pitch pipe is in the meetinghouse cupboard.
WAGON FOR SALE, with the Holt place. One wheel new. Apply to A. Coyle, for the land company.
PIKES, DOWS, HOLTS, MERRILLS, ABBOTTS, LOWELLS. Your animals are in the Varnums' barn. They are fine. The Pikes bite. S. VARNUM
PIKES, DOWS, HOLTS, MERRILLS, ABBOTTS, LOWELLS. Your animals are in the pound on Hobble Hill. They are fine. The Pikes still bite. S. VARNUM

spots.where: by the trough on the common
among the stone rows in Thayer's Yard
in the long grass of the Stone Lane's orchard
by Mr. Coyle's stakes on the Sheep Walk
outside the pound gate on Hobble Hill
under the birch with the chain in it, on the Ox Road
by the cutters' shanty at the Quarry
by the schoolhouse step at Hemlock Brook
by the north farm's cellar hole

thanks: That'll do. Hold still while I find you something.
Good. Put it on the table.
Thank you. Mind the hem on your way out.

notices.title: A Coat, Let Out
notices.payWords: a coat nobody came back for
notices.text: I let a coat out for a man who said he'd be back for it. That was spring. See off two lots in {in} and it's yours.

notices.title: My Thimble
notices.text: Lost my thimble {where}. Brass, worn through on one side. I've been pushing with a spoon.

notices.title: The Button Tin
notices.text: Dropped the button tin {where}. A button off every coat that went down the road. I'd like it back.

notices.title: A Pincushion
notices.text: My pincushion is {where}. I know because somebody saw it there and didn't pick it up.

notices.title: The Full Inch
notices.got: The full inch. She said that last time.
notices.text: Truman Shattuck's good trousers, let out. Tell him it's the full inch and there isn't another.

notices.title: Taken Up
notices.got: For walking. Tell her thank you.
notices.text: Lucy Shattuck's skirt, taken up for walking. Walking where, she didn't say. Take it over.

notices.title: For the Lining
notices.text: Wanted: two hare's feet, off the hares on the Sheep Walk. They go in a lining, for a long walk. My mother did it.

notices.title: Buttons, Copper
notices.text: Wanted: two copper buttons. The fishers on the Ox Road collect them. Don't ask me where they get them.

notices.title: The Washing
notices.text: Something from {in} has been at the washing. Mine and everybody's, and there isn't so much of everybody's now. Two lots, if you would.

notices.title: The South Road
notices.text: Some families go out by the south road, through {in}. I'd like it clear when they do. All of it.

thanks: Obliged. My father'd have done it himself, mind.
That's done, then. It might not have been.

notices.title: Stone Gloves
notices.text: My father wore these clearing the low field. Eleven years. They're good for eleven more. See off two lots in {in} and they're yours.

notices.title: My Whetstone
notices.text: My whetstone is {where}. I set it down. I don't recall setting it down there.

notices.title: The Brindle's Halter
notices.text: The brindle cow's halter came off and was found {where}. She wasn't in it. She's home. The halter isn't.

notices.title: One or Two Changes
notices.got: One or two. He's crossed out half the page.
notices.text: Take this to Lucy. It's the list of what goes. I've made one or two changes.

notices.title: A Can of Milk
notices.got: Set it by the stove. Tell him thank you.
notices.text: Can of milk for Tamsin Gove. She's at the meetinghouse. Don't swing it.

notices.title: Two Good Stones
notices.text: Wanted: two good wall stones, for a gap in the low field wall. I won't take one off another man's wall. Not even an empty farm's.

notices.title: The Low Field
notices.text: Things from {in} have been coming down at night and getting into the low field. See off two lots. My father spent eleven years on that field.

notices.title: It Might
notices.text: I'd like {in} cleared. All of it. I might go up there one more time. I might not.

writers.signed: L. Shattuck, the house with the wagon
thanks: Thank you. One thing done in this house, anyway.
Good. I'll cross it off. I keep a list.
There. Now if only everything stayed done.

notices.title: A Sunday Belt
notices.text: Truman's Sunday belt. He doesn't go to meeting now. Nobody does. See off two lots in {in} and it's yours. He won't miss it.

notices.title: A Bell for Hosea
notices.text: Hosea Lamb's lead ewe came in without her bell. He thinks it's {where}. He won't leave off counting, so I said I'd put it up. Not the old flat one on the Sheep Walk. His rings.

notices.title: The Good Spoon
notices.text: The good spoon is {where}. Packed, unpacked, and gone. If you find the rest of the drawer, leave it.

notices.title: A Pie
notices.got: She knows I'd give it to Obed. Tell her I'll eat half.
notices.text: A pie for Tamsin Gove. She sews all day and forgets. Don't let her give it to Obed Thayer.

notices.title: His Dinner
notices.got: I wasn't thinking. I was resting. Tell her that.
notices.text: Take Truman his dinner. He's in the yard, thinking. He's been thinking since Tuesday.

notices.title: For the Cows
notices.text: Wanted: three witch hazel, for the cows, in the cold. The skunks at Hemlock Brook carry it about. I don't know why and I don't want to.

notices.title: The Cows
notices.text: The cows came home from {in} at a run last night. Something's out there. Two lots, I'd say.

notices.title: Cross It Off
notices.text: Clear {in}, if you would. All of it. It's been on my list since spring, and I'd like one thing on that list crossed off.
